static_traits.name: Chen Jie
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with peers affected by insufficient confidence; has music-circle friends but difficulty opening up to seek support
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no previous counseling or psychiatric treatment history; no history of similar problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good organization, able to self-Reflect; high cooperation, slightly tense but overall positive

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling overwhelmed and inferior from simultaneously Learning and teaching multiple instruments, believing small hands will forever prevent mastering any instrument; this sense of inadequacy frequently appears and worsens during teaching and performance, affecting teaching effectiveness, sleep and focus, and straining relationships with peers.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to change unreasonable negative thinking through counseling, testing the belief that 'small hands = unable to master', regaining passion and confidence for music and teaching.
growth_experiences: After starting to Learn multiple instruments and comparing with others, gradually formed the sense of inadequacy and Self-doubt that 'I am inferior, small hands are a permanent obstacle'; as difficulty and comparison increased, struggling to see one's own progress, Sense of frustration and Worsened self-negation, negative evaluations repeatedly appearing during performance and teaching.

Last year participated in a violin solo concert; after thorough preparation performed excellently, received much praise from the audience, felt confident and recognized that day; this experience suggests thorough practice and positive feedback can significantly boost Self-efficacy.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough/inferior to others
My physical limitations determine my ability and worth

special_situations.event: Not reaching certain notes when teaching piano, with Students auditing/Learning in front
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If technical mistakes appear in front of Students, it shows I am an incompetent teacher
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling practice, seeking comfort and affirmation from colleagues to ease Anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I teach poorly, I will never master it

special_situations.event: After class, watching videos of performers with bigger hands and comparing
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others do it more easily with better conditions, I will never possibly reach their level
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces in-depth exchanges with peers to avoid being compared or evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am inferior to them, I am destined never to reach their level

special_situations.event: Before and after performances and teaching, repeatedly thinks 'small hands are a permanent obstacle'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Innate physical limitations will determine that I cannot master any instrument
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Seeking assurance from others in advance, over-practicing to hedge unease
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My small hands will always hold me back, the future will also fail

special_situations.event: Receiving positive feedback or recalling successful performances (e.g., last year's praised violin solo)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If success cannot last, it does not count as real ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring or downplaying positive evidence, focusing on inadequacy to 'push oneself'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That was just luck, not representing that I am truly capable

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and appreciated, becoming a competent and respected Musician and Teacher
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being negated and humiliated due to physical limitations, unable to handle Teacher and performer roles
defense_goal: Preventing shame brought by external criticism through self-criticism and negation
Temporarily easing Anxiety by seeking others' assurance and over-practicing
Reduces in-depth contact with peers to avoid being compared and judged

object_relations.self_representation: A restricted, error-prone teacher/performer who needs to prove oneself

object_relations.object_representation: Supportive, appreciative audiences/peers who give positive feedback

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor emphasizes one's successful experiences or invites recalling positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing these successes are accidental and unsustainable, worrying the counselor is overly optimistic, not understanding one's 'limitations'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone calm but with Self-denial, using words like 'just coincidental' 'does not count' to lightly downplay success.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests seeking support from peers or friends, openly expressing Self-doubt
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worried that exposing vulnerability will be judged or looked down on, attributing inner self-criticism to others' thoughts
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Evasively avoiding, emphasizing 'they are busy' 'saying it is useless', and trying to change the topic or focus on technical details.

manifestations: Tense relationships with peers due to insufficient confidence, difficulty opening up to friends about Self-doubt
outcomes: Feeling isolated and helpless on the professional path
Worsening Self-doubt and Anxiety, negative thinking cycle

manifestations: Sense of inadequacy affecting passion for music and teaching
Positive experiences quickly negated, difficulty gaining lasting meaning from achievements
outcomes: Decreased motivation, sleep and Impaired concentration

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently Self-denial in sessions, emphasizing 'I am not good enough' 'never able to master'
Worries excessively about others' evaluations before making decisions and shrinks self-expression

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Could have sought help from friends but chose to practice alone harder to hedge Anxiety
Turns the energy of expecting others' support into self-pressure and excessive practice

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: When talking about peers, assumes 'they are better and will look down on me', thus reducing communication
Attributes inner self-criticism experiences to others' judgments

exception_events.target_problem: In performance situations, Chen Jie typically feels inadequate due to Self-doubt and the 'small hands' belief, worrying about poor performance, struggling to present steadily.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In a violin solo last year, Chen Jie prepared fully, performed excellently on site, and received much praise, experiencing strong confidence and a sense of control.
exception_events.reason: Clue: adopted fuller practice and preparation; obtained on-site positive feedback; task focus clear, reducing comparison.

exception_events.target_problem: When teaching, Chen Jie typically feels embarrassed and self-blaming due to technical difficulties and Self-doubt, thereby doubting teaching ability.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once in a class, she prepared thoroughly, structure clear, classroom feedback Good, Self-efficacy improved, and did not fall into long-term Self-denial after class.
exception_events.reason: Clue: concrete teaching goals were set, rehearsal was done before class, and concretized feedback from colleagues was obtained promptly.

positive_force: Has solid training and practical foundations; can improve performance through preparation
Open to growth, willing to try recording practice and seeking concrete feedback
Has music-circle friends and potential mentor resources
Having had successful performances and Good teaching experiences, which can serve as self-efficacy evidence
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization and negating the positive
Seeking external assurance and avoiding exposing vulnerability, leading to The support system has difficulty functioning
Sleep disturbed and Decreased attention, worsening performance Anxiety

After watching videos of others playing more easily, makes comparisons

target_behavior.consequence: Worsened inferiority and Anxiety, declining teaching and performance, sleep and Impaired concentration

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive comparison and repeatedly browsing others' performance videos
antecedent: After setbacks in class or practice
Anxious periods before preparing performances or teaching

When facing new challenges or high-standard tasks
